title: Last cycle's plan as a warm start

blocks.text: Finance cut every year of this cycle to $300k. Last cycle's approved plan no longer fits, but most of it is still good, and the planners want the solver to start from it rather than from nothing. Your milestone turns last cycle's plan into a **warm start**: a complete, rule-abiding plan handed to HiGHS as a solution hint. The data is a fictional utility's practice portfolio.

`warm_start.py` gives you milestone 2's model with a reduced rule set (must-do, at-most-once, alternative, precedence-with-lag and yearly budget rows) as `build(snapshot)`, which returns `(model, x)` with `x[(project, year)]` the start variables, plus `solve(model, model_params)`, `plan_of`, `spend` and the rule checker `check(snapshot, plan)`.

rows: last cycle's starts that this cycle's model has a variable for: the project still exists and the year is in its window. A child whose parent is not carried is not carried either (repeat until none is left)

while `check` reports a broken `budget_<year>` row, drop one optional project among those that spend in a broken year: the one with the least NPV (at its planned start) per $k of total cost, ties to the smaller id. A dropped project's children, and theirs, go with it. Never drop a must-do, nor a project with a must-do among its children or their children in the plan (dropping it would take the must-do with it); if only such projects are left, stop and return the plan
`mathopt.ModelSolveParameters(solution_hints=[mathopt.SolutionHint(variable_values=...)])` with a value for every start variable: 1.0 for the plan's starts, 0.0 for all others

blocks.text: A hint changes where the search starts, never the answer: the tests check that the hinted solve reaches the same optimum as the plain one, and that the start you hand over breaks no rule. About twenty-five lines.

cases.says: a retired project, and a start year this cycle's window no longer allows, are left out of the carried plan
the repaired start breaks no rule, the hint carries exactly its starts, and the hinted solve reaches the same optimum as the plain one
the hint is complete: every start variable gets a value, 0 for the starts the plan does not use
the project dropped first is the one with the least NPV per $k, not the least NPV
a project that spends only in years within budget is kept, however little it is worth
a must-do stays even when it is worth the least per $k
dropping a parent drops its child too, so the start breaks no precedence row
a child whose parent has no start variable this cycle is not carried either
a parent whose child is a must-do is never dropped, so the must-do keeps its start
